issues.legal_issue: Abolition and vesting do not end the landlord–tenant relationship before the provisions extinguishing that relationship take effect when the governing law preserves mutual rights and those provisions commence later.
material_facts: The law abolished the inams and vested the land in the State when it first came into force, but only some of its provisions commenced at that time.
The provisions preserving the application of tenancy law and the mutual rights and obligations of inamdars and tenants were in force from the initial commencement.
The provisions directing that rents be paid to the State and extinguishing the landlord–tenant relationship did not take effect until the rest of the law commenced.
issues.conclusion: The landlord–tenant relationship continued after abolition and vesting until the delayed provisions took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(1) and 3(2)(b) and section 33 of the Hyderabad Abolition of Inams Act, 1954, the interests expressly saved from vesting and the mutual rights and obligations under the Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 were preserved. Since sections 3(2)(d), (g), (h) and (i), including the provision extinguishing the relationship, commenced later, the relationship continued until then. Section 4 of the 1956 Amendment Act, which treated the inamdar as an occupant for land-revenue purposes during the interval, supported that reading.

predicates.statutory_inam_abolition_case: The proceeding concerns a law abolishing inam interests and vesting the land in the State.
predicates.mutual_tenancy_rights_preserved: The law preserves the application of tenancy rules and the mutual rights and obligations between the landholder and tenant.
predicates.relationship_extinction_provision_not_ye: The provision ending the landholder–tenant relationship has not yet taken effect.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_continues_u: The landholder–tenant relationship continues until the provision ending it takes effect.

issues.definition: When an abolition law preserves tenancy rights and its relationship-ending provision has not taken effect, the relationship continues until that provision takes effect.

issues.legal_issue: Occupancy rights under a law whose occupancy provisions commence after vesting are determined by who is lawfully in possession when those provisions commence.
material_facts: The occupancy-rights provisions and the provisions ending the landlord–tenant relationship commenced after the initial vesting of the land.

In one appeal, the tenant claimed to remain in possession when the full law commenced, while the inamdar also claimed possession; the authorities had instead relied on possession at the initial vesting.

In the other appeal, the tenant voluntarily surrendered the tenancy before the full law commenced, the inamdar accepted the surrender and remained in possession, but the authorities granted occupancy rights to the tenant based on possession at the initial vesting.
issues.conclusion: The operative date for deciding occupancy rights was the commencement of the full law, not the initial vesting. An inamdar who accepted a tenant’s surrender and remained in possession on that date was entitled to occupancy rights; where both claimed possession, the Government had to determine who was lawfully in possession on that date. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 1(3)(b) and 4 to 8 of the Hyderabad Abolition of Inams Act, 1954 made the commencement of the full law, including the occupancy-rights provisions, decisive. Until then, section 33 preserved the tenancy relationship; the delayed operation of sections 3(2)(d), (g), (h) and (i) likewise supported that result. The Court approved Dattatraya Sadashiv Dhand v. Ganpati Raghu Gaoll, 67 B.L.R. 521, on the continuation of the relationship until the full law commenced.

predicates.occupancy_rights_determination: The proceeding determines who is entitled to occupancy rights in land affected by an abolition law.
predicates.occupancy_provisions_commenced_after_ini: The provisions governing occupancy rights took effect after the land initially vested in the State.
predicates.lawful_possession_on_full_commencement: A person was lawfully in possession of the land when the full occupancy-rights regime took effect.
predicates.occupancy_rights_follow_lawful_possessio: Occupancy rights are awarded according to who was lawfully in possession when the full occupancy-rights regime took effect.

issues.definition: When occupancy-rights provisions take effect after initial vesting, the person lawfully in possession when those provisions take effect receives the occupancy rights.
